title: Manifest
description: The whole manifest. A program asks for the tables it needs; a table nobody declared is an error.

fastboot.description: How the lab reaches the phone over fastboot, and whether it may write to it there

hear.description: what the lab's ear listens for

health.description: what the phone's own health suite expects of it

hazard.description: What must never be touched on this phone, whoever asks

user_config.description: Config files the phone keeps outside any git, which the lab names when they drift (lpoco host check)

host.description: What the lab host needs for this device

boot.description: The header facts of the phone's boot image

layer.description: The device layer: what each package format is generated from

tools.description: The tools this device's lab pins

addresses.description: Addresses to try, in order (USB networking first, as a rule)

checks.description: The checks script, relative to the manifest; run on the phone as root, one JSON line per check

Provision.description: What a freshly flashed phone gets.

packages.description: The package list, relative to the manifest

install.description: Files to install - `{compatible}` is the phone's device-tree name

when.description: A command on the phone that must succeed for the file to go on (empty: always)

Flash.description: How an image goes onto the phone, and what is baked into it.

dtb.description: Where the device tree lives in the image (esp:/... or root:/...), for --dtb and the fingerprint

enable.description: Services enabled on first boot - always, even --as-is (the lab must reach the phone)

Overlay.description:
A file baked into the image: from the lab repository, to esp:/... or root:/...; skipped unless
`if_exists` (also esp:/... or root:/...) exists in the image.

Fastboot.description:
The phone as fastboot knows it. Every fastboot call devlab makes names this serial, so a lab with two
phones in fastboot never reaches the wrong one; and nothing is written over fastboot (flash) unless the
manifest says `writes = true` - a phone whose slots must stay as they are says nothing, or false
(google-walleye: decision 2026-11-17-walleye-fastboot-first).

writes.description: Whether devlab may write partitions over fastboot (devlab flash); false unless said

slot_switch.description:
Whether devlab may change the active slot (devlab fastboot set-active: the bootloader's metadata, no
partition written); false unless a recorded decision says so

Hear.description:
The tones the lab's ear listens for (`devlab hear`); none named means one on each side. How loud
any test sound may be is said here too, quiet by default: a phone in a home must never shout - a
full-scale tone at night once woke the author. Every check that plays sound reads the same two
values (TEST_TONE_DBFS, TEST_VOLUME in the phone's health.env).

level_dbfs.description: the tone's level in the file, dBFS (at most 0)

volume.description: the phone's output volume while a test sound plays, percent (at most 100)

Health.description:
What the phone's own health suite expects of this phone (lpoco-health, on the phone). Every
field is a fact about the hardware; what it says becomes /etc/devlab/health.env there.

sound_cards.description: Sound cards that must be registered: names as /proc/asound/cards shows them

remoteprocs.description: Signal processors that must be running: remoteproc name -> the component that rests on it

known_warnings.description: Kernel warnings known at boot (file:line), each with its reason beside it in the manifest

known_failed_units.description: Units known to fail on this phone, each with its reason beside it in the manifest

absent.description:
Parts this phone does not have at all (wifi, modem, bluetooth, nfc, fingerprint, camera, jack,
display, touchscreen, haptics, sensors, usb-otg): skipped, never failing

gaps.description:
Components this phone has never had working (docs component ids), each with its reason beside it:
still measured and reported, but a failure there is a known gap, not ill health

checks.description: This phone's own checks, relative to the manifest: base/*.sh and shell/*.sh beneath it

data_budget_mb.description:
Mobile data the health checks may spend in a month, in MB (250 when unsaid): the telephony
layer's mobile-data check skips once the month has spent it (lpoco-health data)

suspend_irq_max.description:
Interrupts one 15 s suspended cycle may count in all (the suite check suspend-irq-quiet); unsaid, the
check says not measured: the number comes from a reading of this phone, never a guess

suspend_guard.description:
A command on the phone that succeeds while its watchdog is armed (the way-back check): the suite
suspends only if it does; unsaid, it never suspends

suspend_quiet.description:
Wakeup files (sysfs, e.g. a UART's power/wakeup) put to "disabled" for the controlled suspend cycle
(lpoco-health suspend cycle) and put back after: the wake sources that would end s2idle at once

suspend_stop.description:
Systemd services stopped before the controlled suspend cycle (lpoco-health suspend cycle) and started
again after it, last stopped first: the daemons a suspend would crash or leave stopped (surya: sensorspd)

awake_gates.description:
Gates that hold the keep-awake lock (lpoco-health awake) while autosleep is allowed, named by token:
bluetooth-not-up (hci0 not UP, or an rfkill stuck in D state). The package knows the tokens; an unknown one is refused

Hazard.description: A path on the phone that harms it to touch - each with what it did, so the refusal says why.

UserConfig.description:
A config file on the phone, outside any git, that the lab compares at each check: declared either against
the default its package ships (`expect`, a phone path) or against a copy kept in the base (`from`, a path
in the device repository) - exactly one. A deliberate change then lives in the base or in the package.

path.description: The file's absolute path on the phone

expect.description: The package default's absolute path on the phone, e.g. /usr/share/sxmo/...

from.description: The copy kept in the device repository, relative to the manifest

watch.description: The device asks to be watched: prepare enables its `devlab-watch@` instance. Watching is the device's own choice, like its gadgets.

commands.description: Programs the device needs on the host's PATH: named by plan, judged by check, never installed (installing is a root pacman the author grants).

targets.description: Rust targets the device's tools are built for: named by plan, judged by check (a standard library on the host), never installed.

net_name.description: A stable name for the gadget's USB network interface (CDC-NCM and friends), set by udev at plug-in: the kernel's own name follows the port.

net_address.description: The host's address on that network, as IPv4 CIDR (`10.55.0.1/24`): written as a link config for the host's own network manager, only with the verb. Needs `net_name`.

usb_id.description: What the phone shows on the host's USB bus when this gadget is up, as `vendor:product` in four hex digits each (`18d1:4ee0`); kept lowercase.

Access.description: `devices = "glob"` is the lab's; these are the device's own `[host]` words.

header_version.description: 0 is the only header version this tool packs and checks so far

os_version.description: "A.B.C"; none says the header holds no os words

partition_size.description: the boot partition's size in bytes: an image must fit it

msm_id.description: the qcom,msm-id words the appended device tree must carry

hooks.description: step name to executable (relative to the manifest): `parts` runs on kernel and ramdisk before packing

gadget.description: the USB gadget the bring-up init (`lpoco-bringup initramfs init`) raises: how the phone names itself on the cable

BootGadget.description:
`[boot.gadget]`: what the bring-up init says of the phone on the USB cable. The functions (ACM serial
console, ECM network, RNDIS for Windows hosts) and the address (`--net`) are the init's; the names are the device's.

serial.description: the gadget's USB serial number string (the lab finds the phone by it)

label.description: the word the init's log lines start with (`LABEL: up, kernel ...`)

rndis.description: a second configuration, RNDIS + ACM, for Windows hosts

window.description: a read-only mass-storage LUN the host can read: the init keeps the phone's kernel log and uptime written into it (a log window when the phone has no network yet)

console.description: the serial console: `acm` (the kernel's ACM function, default) or `ffs` (the `ffs-acm` helper over FunctionFS: one interface without CDC descriptors, for kernels whose ACM function is missing; the helper must be in the ramdisk as /bin/ffs-acm and it binds the UDC itself)

Console.description: Which serial console the bring-up init raises.

name.description: the packages' stem: NAME-config, NAME-boot, linux-NAME

needs.description: dependency tokens ("qrtr", "tqftpserv>=1.2"); a token map names each per base

names.description: the token map: per format, the package name a token has there when it is not the token itself

file.description: the files the layer installs, each with its kind and a destination under /usr

LayerNames.description: `[layer.names.FORMAT]`: token = "that format's package name"; a token not listed keeps its own name.

LayerKernel.description: `[layer.kernel]`: where the kernel comes from and what it builds.

config.description: a config fragment over the architecture's defconfig, relative to the manifest

dtbs.description: device trees installed, relative to the kernel's dts directory

BootMethod.description: How the phone's kernel is started; `android-bootimg` takes its addresses from `[boot]`.

FirmwareMethod.description: Where firmware comes from: the OEM's is never packaged, only extracted from the phone's own partitions.

LayerInitramfs.description: `[layer.initramfs]`: one module list, a drop-in per initramfs tool.

Tools.description: `[tools]`: the pins of this device's lab.

lpoco.description: The release of the lpoco family the phone's pieces come from
